themes.title: Angelology and Spiritual Warfare
themes.description: This theme covers the nature, hierarchy, and roles of angels and demons, including the divine council, the fall of angels, and the ongoing spiritual battle between God and evil forces. It also explores the identification of pagan gods with fallen angels and the practical means of resisting demonic influence.

themes.title: Christology and Incarnation
themes.description: This theme focuses on the person and work of Jesus Christ, including His pre-incarnate appearances in the Old Testament, His incarnation, crucifixion, resurrection, and ascension. It explores His role as the Messiah, the fulfillment of Old Testament types, and His victory over death and the devil.

themes.title: Atonement and Sacrifice
themes.description: This theme explores the biblical understanding of sacrifice, atonement, and purification, including the Day of Atonement, the Eucharist, and the crucifixion of Christ. It contrasts penal substitution with participatory and cosmic atonement, emphasizing the victory over sin and death.

themes.title: Theosis and Deification
themes.description: This theme covers the Orthodox understanding of salvation as becoming partakers of the divine nature, becoming like God, and joining the heavenly hosts. It emphasizes the transformative process of theosis, the role of the Incarnation, and the ultimate destiny of humanity.

themes.title: Divine Council and Angelic Hierarchy
themes.description: This theme explores the heavenly assembly of spiritual beings over which God presides, including the ranks and roles of angels, and the biblical concept of 'gods' as members of this council. It also covers the fall of some angels and the ongoing spiritual warfare.

themes.title: Spiritual Warfare and Demonic Forces
themes.description: This theme addresses the reality of demonic powers, their influence on individuals and societies, and the Christian response through spiritual warfare. It includes demonic possession, the 'world' as a demonic social order, and the power of baptism and the Eucharist in overcoming evil.

themes.title: Sacraments and Liturgy
themes.description: This theme covers the sacramental life of the Church, including baptism, chrismation, Eucharist, confession, ordination, and marriage. It explores their biblical roots, theological meaning, and practical implications for the life of the Church, as well as the liturgical context in which they are celebrated.

themes.title: Scripture and Hermeneutics
themes.description: This theme explores how Scripture is interpreted within the Orthodox tradition, emphasizing the role of the Church Fathers, the Holy Spirit, and the principle of trust in bishops. It addresses the dangers of liberal theology and the importance of reading Scripture in the context of the Church.

themes.title: Creation and the Cosmos
themes.description: This theme covers the biblical view of creation, including the spiritual realities of the sea, the deep, and the heavenly bodies, and the re-enchantment of science. It explores the relationship between God, humanity, and the cosmos, and the human vocation to continue the work of ordering creation.

themes.title: Eschatology and the Afterlife
themes.description: This theme covers the final things: the Second Coming, the resurrection of the dead, the Last Judgment, and the eternal state. It explores the biblical imagery of the Day of the Lord, the Millennium, the Antichrist, and the final defeat of evil, emphasizing the present reality of the Messianic Age and the hope of bodily resurrection.

themes.title: Theology of God and Trinity
themes.description: This theme explores the nature of God, the Trinity, and the relationship between the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. It includes discussions of the two powers in heaven, the hypostases, and the incarnation, as well as the distinction between God's essence and energies.

themes.title: Anthropology and Human Person
themes.description: This theme explores the nature of the human person as body and soul, the image of God, and the effects of the Fall on human nature. It critiques Platonic dualism and emphasizes the soul as the life of the body, with eternal life defined as knowing God.

themes.title: Paganism and Idolatry
themes.description: This theme examines the biblical polemic against pagan deities and practices, showing how Scripture subverts and reinterprets ancient Near Eastern mythology. It includes the Baal Cycle, divine smack talk, and the inversion of pagan rituals, as well as the Christian response to pagan religion.

themes.title: Saints and the Theotokos
themes.description: This theme covers the veneration of saints and relics, the concept of theosis, and the belief that saints become places where God dwells. It includes the theological foundations for relics and the intercession of the saints, with special focus on the Virgin Mary as the Theotokos and Queen Mother.

themes.title: Old Testament Foundations
themes.description: This theme covers the historical and theological foundations of the Old Testament, including the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings, and how they are interpreted in light of Christ and the New Testament. It includes discussions of the Exodus, the Law, the temple, and the priesthood.

themes.title: Church and Ecclesiology
themes.description: This theme explores the nature of the Church as the body of Christ, the priesthood of all believers, and the importance of community and tradition. It covers the Church's structure, the role of bishops and priests, and the relationship between doctrine and practice.

themes.title: Spiritual Life and Practice
themes.description: This theme covers the practices and disciplines of the Christian life, including prayer, fasting, almsgiving, and the pursuit of theosis. It emphasizes the importance of asceticism, the struggle against passions, and the goal of union with God.

themes.title: Prophecy and Apocalyptic
themes.description: This theme explores the genre of apocalypse as revelation, the prophetic tradition, and the Day of the Lord. It includes the role of prophets like Elijah and John the Forerunner, and the unveiling of spiritual realities behind historical events.

themes.title: Time and Eternity
themes.description: This theme explores the nature of time from an Orthodox perspective, arguing that God is not bound by time and that time is a phenomenological experience of creatures. It critiques views like Calvinism and open theism that presuppose God's temporality, and discusses the liturgical calendar as a means of theosis.

themes.title: Election and Predestination
themes.description: This theme discusses the biblical concept of election (being chosen) in light of Orthodox theology, rejecting Calvinist double predestination and open theism. It emphasizes that God's foreknowledge is not deterministic and that election is corporate and Christ-centered.

themes.title: Modernity and Culture
themes.description: This theme critiques modern and postmodern concepts of religion, individualism, and progress, contrasting them with the Orthodox understanding of religion as a way of being in the world. It examines the Axial Age and the Neolithic Revolution as historical shifts that shaped religious practice and belief.

themes.title: Second Temple Judaism
themes.description: This theme situates Christianity within the context of Second Temple Judaism, emphasizing its continuity with Jewish apocalyptic and wisdom traditions. It discusses the diversity of Jewish beliefs about angels, demons, and the afterlife, and how early Christianity emerged as a Jewish movement.

themes.title: Ethics and Moral Theology
themes.description: This theme engages with philosophical and theological questions about the nature of good and evil, the basis of morality, and the role of divine commands. It critiques modern ethical theories and presents an Orthodox Christian alternative centered on participation in God's energies.

themes.title: History and Tradition
themes.description: This theme explores the Orthodox understanding of history as sacred narrative and the role of tradition in preserving the faith. It covers the history of the Church, the ecumenical councils, and the development of doctrine.

themes.title: The Fall and Original Sin
themes.description: This theme explores the biblical account of the fall of humanity and angels, the origin of death and mortality, and the consequences for the world. It covers the roles of Adam, Cain, and the Tower of Babel, and the impact of sin on the cosmos.
